page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-128GB is a memory-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 shared x86_64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it is provisioned with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between raw compute power and memory capacity. The shared CPU allocation results in poor single-core and weak multi-core CPU performance under stress-ng testing, placing it in the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. However, memory bandwidth benchmarks for both small and large blocks remain in the average range. General processing tasks, such as software compilation, image processing, and text processing, perform at average levels, as indicated by Geekbench and Passmark metrics.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a high density of memory resources relative to its compute allocation, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained, high-performance CPU cores. It is well-suited for database operations, Redis caching layers, and static web serving, where memory capacity is prioritized over raw processing speed. Conversely, it is poorly suited for demanding compute tasks like medium-to-large language model inference, where text generation speeds fall into the bottom 10%.
